entities.title: Each map holds a set number of agents
entities.summary: The Safehouse holds 2 agents, the Embassy 4, the Grand Hotel Meridian 6 and Polar Station Kappa 8.
entities.statement: The briefing room refuses to start a match with more agents than the chosen map holds; spectators don't count.
entities.rationale: The owner asked for maps with different maximum player counts.
acceptanceCriteria: With 5 agents ready, the Embassy can't be started and the briefing room says why.
Choosing to spectate frees a place.

origin.description: The owner's request for the game.

entities.title: Two ways to play
entities.summary: Last Agent Standing (everyone for themselves) and Co-op Teams (two teams that pool their intel and can't hurt each other).
entities.statement: The host picks the mode. In Last Agent Standing the last agent alive wins, or the first to reach the extraction door with all four pieces of intel. In Co-op Teams a team wins when any member reaches the door while the team's living members hold all four between them, or when the other team is eliminated.
entities.rationale: The owner asked for co-op teams and last-man-standing modes.
acceptanceCriteria: Teammates take no damage from each other's punches or traps.
An agent at the door without all the intel is told what is still missing.

origin.description: The owner's request for the game.

entities.title: The eliminated keep watching
entities.summary: An agent who dies enters spectator mode, which shows every surviving agent at once.
entities.statement: After elimination the screen becomes a grid with one live camera per surviving agent, every trap revealed; Tab switches to one agent full screen and back. Anyone can also join as a spectator from the briefing room.
entities.rationale: The owner asked for a spectator mode showing all players, entered on death.
acceptanceCriteria: With three agents alive, a spectator sees three tiles.
When one of them dies, the grid rebuilds with two.

origin.description: The owner's request for the game.

entities.title: Every agent on their own screen
entities.summary: Each player plays on their own device; nobody shares a screen.
entities.statement: Online, each browser follows its own agent and lights only the room that agent is in; other agents are visible only in that room or its doorways.
entities.rationale: The owner asked for multiplayer on separate screens.
acceptanceCriteria: An agent in another room is hidden.
Teammates show on the minimap; opponents never do.
